course: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)
chapterTitle: Put-Call Parity, Arbitrage Strategies, Merton's Capital Structure Model, and Early Exercise Properties

beatOutlines.textOutline: A quantitative trader notices that European calls and puts on the same non-dividend-paying stock with strike K and maturity T must obey Put-Call Parity: c + K*e^(-rT) = p + S_0 ([fact-01]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A mentor explains the replication proof using two portfolios: Portfolio A (1 call + cash K*e^(-rT)) and Portfolio B (1 put + 1 stock share) ([fact-02]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: They verify that both portfolios yield the exact same terminal payoff max(S_T, K) at expiration T in all market states, enforcing parity via the Law of One Price ([fact-02]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Replication Cash Flows at Expiration T

beatOutlines.textOutline: Display Portfolio A terminal cash flows at T: if S_T > K, call pays (S_T - K) + K = S_T; if S_T <= K, call pays 0 + K = K ([fact-01], [fact-02]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Display Portfolio B terminal cash flows at T: if S_T > K, stock is worth S_T and put is 0; if S_T <= K, put exercises stock to K, matching Portfolio A's max(S_T, K) payoff exactly ([fact-02]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Pillar 1: Put-Call Parity & Replication — Mathematical parity equation and Law of One Price proof using Portfolios A and B ([fact-01]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Pillar 2: Arbitrage Execution — Fiduciary Call and Reversal arbitrage steps when parity is violated ([fact-03]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Pillar 3: Merton's Capital Structure Model — Corporate equity as a call option and debt as a risk-free bond minus a put ([fact-05]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Pillar 4: Early Exercise Properties — Why American calls are never exercised early (C = c) while deep-ITM American puts can be ([fact-07]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Fiduciary Call Arbitrage vs. Reversal Arbitrage

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Fiduciary Call Arbitrage (when c + K*e^(-rT) > p + S_0): sell call, buy put, buy stock, borrow discounted strike K*e^(-rT) to lock in positive upfront cash ([fact-03]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Reversal Arbitrage (when c + K*e^(-rT) < p + S_0): buy call, sell put, short stock, lend/invest discounted strike K*e^(-rT) to lock in riskless cash profit ([fact-04]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Arbitrage Liability Cancellation at Expiration T

beatOutlines.textOutline: Show Fiduciary Call expiration mechanics: loan repayment of -K is perfectly offset by +K from short call exercise (if S_T > K) or long put exercise (if S_T <= K), leaving zero net liability ([fact-03]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Show Reversal expiration mechanics: investment grows to +K, which exactly pays -K to buy stock and close short stock position via long call or short put assignment ([fact-04]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Merton's Model: Equity as a Call & Debt as Bond Minus Put

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Equity Payoff E_T = max(V_T - D, 0): equity is a European call on firm assets V with strike D, defaulting to 0 if V_T <= D due to limited liability ([fact-05]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Debt Payoff min(V_T, D) = D - max(D - V_T, 0): corporate debt equals a risk-free bond paying D minus a short European put on firm value V with strike D ([fact-06]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: American Call Early Exercise Prohibition (C = c)

beatOutlines.textOutline: Analyze Reason 1 (Time Value of Money): delaying strike payment K until T earns risk-free interest over (T - t), making waiting superior to early exercise ([fact-07]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Analyze Reason 2 & 3 (Downside Insurance & Selling Dominance): holding calls provides downside protection, and since C >= c >= S_t - K*e^(-r(T-t)) > S_t - K, selling the call in the market always yields more than early exercise ([fact-07]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: American Put Early Exercise: Time Value vs. Insurance Value

beatOutlines.textOutline: Illustrate the tug-of-war for American puts: Benefit of early exercise (immediate receipt of cash strike K to earn risk-free interest) versus Cost (forfeiting downside insurance value if stock rebounds) ([fact-08]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Show that when stock price S_0 drops deep ITM near zero below critical barrier S*, insurance value becomes negligible, making early exercise optimal ([fact-08]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Plot max(S_T, K) payoff for Put-Call Parity replication portfolios A and B, demonstrating identical terminal value across all spot prices ([fact-02]).

beatOutlines.textOutline: Plot Merton's capital structure curves: equity call max(V_T - D, 0) alongside debt payoff min(V_T, D) across firm asset values V_T ([fact-05], [fact-06]).

scenes.title: 8-Step Mastery Thread: Parity, Arbitrage, Merton & Early Exercise

beatOutlines.textOutline: Synthesize Steps 1 to 4: Put-Call Parity formula c + K*e^(-rT) = p + S_0 ([fact-01]), replication proof via Portfolios A and B yielding max(S_T, K) ([fact-02]), Fiduciary Call Arbitrage for overpriced calls ([fact-03]), and Reversal Arbitrage for underpriced calls ([fact-04]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: 1. Put-Call Parity Equation ([fact-01]): For European options on non-dividend-paying stock, c + K*e^(-rT) = p + S_0 links call and put prices through discounted strike present value.
2. Replication Law of One Price ([fact-02]): Portfolio A (call + discounted cash) and Portfolio B (put + stock) both yield identical terminal payoff max(S_T, K) at maturity T.
3. Fiduciary Call Arbitrage ([fact-03]): When c + K*e^(-rT) > p + S_0, shorting the call, buying the put, buying the stock, and borrowing the discounted strike locks in riskless upfront profit.
4. Reversal Arbitrage ([fact-04]): When c + K*e^(-rT) < p + S_0, buying the call, shorting the put, shorting the stock, and lending the discounted strike locks in riskless cash profit.
5. Merton's Equity Call Model ([fact-05]): Corporate equity is structured as a European call option on firm asset value V with strike D, defaulting to 0 if V_T <= D due to limited liability.
6. Merton's Debt as Bond Minus Put ([fact-06]): Corporate debt payoff min(V_T, D) is economically equivalent to a risk-free bond paying D minus a short European put on firm value V.

7. American Call Early Exercise Prohibition ([fact-07]): American calls on non-dividend stocks are never exercised early (C = c) due to time value of money, insurance value, and the dominance of selling over exercising.
8. American Put Early Exercise Conditions ([fact-08]): Deep-in-the-money American puts can be optimal to exercise early when spot price approaches zero below critical barrier S*.
bottomTakeaway: Put-Call Parity links European options through arbitrage replication portfolios, Merton's model frames corporate capital structure as asset options, and non-dividend American calls are never exercised early unlike deep-ITM puts ([fact-01], [fact-02], [fact-03], [fact-04], [fact-05], [fact-06], [fact-07], [fact-08]).
